key_insight: X-ray absorption and DFT+U show that oxygen vacancies in NdBaCo2O5+δ are likely distributed beyond the usual apical sites, helping explain magnetic inhomogeneity and variable-range-hopping transport.
engineering_relevance: Controlling vacancy ordering in layered cobaltates could improve oxygen-ion mobility and enable faster, more sensitive oxygen-sensor materials.
method: Measured Co K, Ba LIII, and Nd LIII edge XANES spectra
Compared spectral features with multiple-scattering simulations and DFT+U calculations
Used edge-shape/feature analysis to infer vacancy distribution and oxidation states
evidence_signal: The near-edge spectra indicate δ is closer to 0.75 than the nominal ~0.65, and Ba is confirmed as +2 while Co-edge features suggest mixed vacancy locations.
watch_item: The vacancy-location interpretation is spectroscopic and model-dependent, so direct structural validation is still needed before device optimization.
paper_title: X-ray absorption spectroscopic studies of oxygen-deficient double perovskite oxide NdBaCo$_2$O$_{5+δ}$ ($δ\sim 0.65$)
